items.stem: Mang Jun can wash the ambulance fleet in 18 hours. Datu can do the same job in 9 hours. Working together, how long will they take?

reveal.terms: A "rate" is how much of the job gets done in one hour.
reveal.shortcut: Per hour, Mang Jun does 1/18 and Datu does 1/9. Together: 1/18 + 1/9 = 1/6. So the whole job takes 6 hours.
reveal.why_correct: 6 hours is right. Check: in 6 hours, Mang Jun does 6/18 and Datu does 6/9; together that is 1 whole job.

why_wrong.o2: This reads the combined rate (1/6 of the job per hour) as a time. It stops before turning the rate into hours.
why_wrong.o3: 13.5 hours is the average of the two times. Together they must be faster than the faster person alone.
why_wrong.o4: 27 hours adds the two times. Add the work done per hour, not the hours.

options.text: Engr. Carlos T. De los Santos

reveal.terms: "Indexing" means writing a name in filing order: surname first, then given name, then middle initial. A title such as Dr. is the last unit.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite each surname as one block: drop spaces and hyphens, keep the prefix (Dela Cruz = DELACRUZ). Then compare letter by letter (ARMA Rule 1). Order: Elena P. Delos Reyes → DELOSREYES, Elena; Engr. Carlos T. De los Santos → DELOSSANTOS, Carlos; Felipe D. Leon → LEON, Felipe; Atty. Danilo F. Rosario → ROSARIO, Danilo.
reveal.why_correct: "Elena P. Delos Reyes" is right. It comes first when every name is indexed surname first, letter by letter. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 6), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o1: "Engr. Carlos T. De los Santos" sorts by the given name. Personal names file by surname first.
why_wrong.o2: "Atty. Danilo F. Rosario" sorts by the title (Dr., Atty., Engr.). A title is only the last unit.
why_wrong.o4: "Felipe D. Leon" files the prefix as a separate word (for example "Dela Cruz" under C). A prefix joins the rest of the surname.

reveal.terms: "Indexing" means writing a name in filing order: surname first, then given name, then middle initial. A title such as Dr. is the last unit.
reveal.shortcut: Rewrite each surname as one block: drop spaces and hyphens, keep the prefix (Dela Cruz = DELACRUZ). Then compare letter by letter (ARMA Rule 1). Order: Corazon C. reveal.why_correct: "Corazon C. Delos Reyes" is right. It comes first when every name is indexed surname first, letter by letter. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 6), not a rule published by the CSC. Source standard: ANSI/ARMA 12-2005.

why_wrong.o2: "Eduardo P. Salazar" files as SALAZAR, which comes after DELOSREYES.
